title: Pluggable audit sink orchestration with consistency models
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a pluggable audit sink orchestration layer (the 'sink-multiplexer') that routes audit events to multiple external targets (Splunk, Datadog, generic webhook proxies) with configurable delivery guarantees and failover semantics. The mux must support per-tenant sink configs, ordered vs best-effort delivery modes, idempotent retries, at-least-once vs exactly-once (best-effort) documentation, and observability hooks for SLA enforcement.

Scope: connector framework, ack/nack/circuit-breaker policies, per-tenant backpressure and quotas, persistent DLQ for undeliverable batches, TLS and KMS integration for endpoint secrets, metrics and tracing, migration plan from current simple forwarder. Not in scope: building new proprietary SIEM adapters (we'll use Splunk/Datadog official SDKs and a generic webhook contract).
design_notes:
Core design choices: use a routing abstraction with connector plugins (gRPC interface) that expose bulk_send(batch) -> ack/nack semantics. The multiplexer will maintain a small persistent send-queue per tenant+sink to preserve ordering when ordered mode enabled. For throughput we will allow configurable batching windows and a continuous batching path for low latency paths.

Consistency models: 1) Ordered-At-Least-Once (default for customers with ordering requirement) — per-tenant sequence + persistent queue + retries + DLQ. 2) Unordered-At-Least-Once — best throughput, worker pool, no per-tenant single-writer. 3) Best-Effort / Fire-and-Forget — webhooks where customers accept potential loss for lower cost.

Retries: exponential backoff with jitter, per-sink limits, and a backoff-aware token bucket to avoid amplification. Circuit breaker states (closed, open, half-open) persisted in Redis with TTL and reset policy. Idempotency: events carry a stable event_id + dedup window implemented by connector that can be backed by Redis or local LRU depending on tenant scale.

Security: connector credentials are stored in KMS-wrapped secrets; transport TLS 1.3 enforced. Audit payloads are signed with a rotating key for customer verification if requested.

Trade-offs: Exactly-once semantics are infeasible without sink-side support; we will document the strongest practical guarantees and provide patterns for downstream reconciliation. The persistent per-tenant queue increases storage and recovery complexity but is required for ordered mode and customer RPOs.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Multiplexer can register 3 connector types (splunk-hec, datadog-http, generic-webhook) and route to them based on tenant config.
2) Ordered delivery mode preserves event order for a tenant across retries and restarts (validated by chaos test).
3) System exposes observability: per-sink success rate, p50/p95 send latency, retry counts, DLQ fill-rate.
4) On a simulated 500 TPS audit stream, default batching path maintains p95 end-to-end latency < 250ms and throughput within 10% of baseline.
5) Failover policy: if primary sink fails, the mux fails over to configured secondary within 5s (configurable).
6) Documentation and runbook for tenants to opt-in/out of ordered mode, configure retries, and interpret DLQ artifacts.
7) Security review completed and KMS integration verified in staging.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for connector interface and retry/backoff logic.
- Integration tests with Splunk HEC mock and Datadog mock endpoints.
- Chaos testing: kill multiplexer process, restart, validate no reordering for ordered tenants.
- Load test: 1k TPS synthetic producer across 100 tenants to validate batching windows and resource usage.
- Backpressure test: simulate a slow sink (2000ms) to verify circuit breaker and token bucket prevent system-wide degradation.
- DLQ validation: produce permanent 4xx failures and validate items land in DLQ with clear reasons.
- Security tests: verify TLS, secret rotation, and signed payload verification.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flagged deploy to staging (end-to-end connectors enabled). 2) Canary to 5% of tenants in prod using new mux with best-effort mode only. Monitor metrics for 48h. 3) Enable ordered mode for internal test tenants and SOC-owned customers. 4) Gradually onboard customers with explicit opt-in and update docs. 5) Full rollout once metrics stable for 7 days and incident rate zero.

Migration notes: existing forwarder will be kept as a compatibility shim for 60 days; a one-time migration job will backfill undelivered items to per-tenant queues if requested by customers.
